subject.title: feat(google-meet): retain the full caption transcript per session (#103387)

question: After bounding completed-session memory, should Google Meet ship a runtime-memory-only transcript API with restart loss and 2000-line eviction, or require persistent plugin-owned SQLite storage first?
rationale: The lifecycle defect is repairable, but durability and irreversible eviction are user-visible product semantics that tests cannot decide.

options.title: Approve bounded memory
options.body: Add ended-session expiry or a historical-session cap, document restart and eviction loss, and land after live proof.

options.title: Require SQLite durability
options.body: Pause the public retrieval API until plugin-owned persistence and restart recovery are implemented.

options.title: Defer transcript retrieval
options.body: Keep the existing recent-transcript surface and postpone full transcript retrieval.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded memory
recommendation.body: Add ended-session expiry or a historical-session cap, document restart and eviction loss, and land after live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Feature history ties this person to the plugin introduction, caption observer, and current session-runtime behavior.
